slides.text: My husband Elias is a brilliant defense attorney, famous for getting the city's worst scum acquitted. He always claimed he could spot a liar from a mile away. So, when the police found his rich, arrogant client murdered, Elias was devastated. I held him as he cried on our living room sofa. 'I know he was guilty of many things,' Elias sobbed into my shoulder, 'but no one deserves to be butchered with a knife like that.'

I stroked his hair, making soothing noises until he fell into an exhausted sleep. I quietly stood up and walked to the kitchen to pour myself a glass of wine. The evening news was playing silently on the small counter TV. The breaking news ticker caught my eye. The police had just held a press conference regarding his client's murder. I turned up the volume, sipping my red wine as the grim-faced detective spoke.

'We are withholding the cause of death from the public,' the detective announced. 'Only the killer knows that the victim was actually poisoned.' The wine glass slipped from my hand, shattering on the tile floor. I slowly turned back toward the dark living room. Elias was no longer asleep on the sofa. He was standing in the doorway to the kitchen, holding a very sharp steak knife. 'You should have just gone to bed, darling,' he whispered.
